roe.text: Nahiri, Sorin Markov and Ugin decided to rid the Multiverse of the Eldrazi, but could not defeat them, so they chose to imprison them on Nahiri's Zendikar instead.
Sorin lured the Eldrazi, Ugin bound them with colorless magic, and Nahiri built the hedron network that formed the bars of their prison.
Once the titans were confined and sank into dormancy, the planeswalkers disbanded, and Nahiri stayed behind to guard the prison.
When vampires built a shrine that destabilized the prison, Nahiri woke, called for help in vain, and restored it alone before leaving to find Sorin.

avr.text: Nahiri's story in Avacyn Restored begins long before, when she sought Sorin's aid and, provoked, he had Avacyn imprison her in the Helvault.
Freed when the Helvault was sundered, she returned to a ravaged Zendikar, grew embittered, and swore vengeance on Sorin.
She destroyed Markov Manor, built cryptoliths and the Drownyard Temple, and summoned Emrakul to Innistrad, and the power of those cryptoliths drove Avacyn and many other angels mad.
Nahiri then wounded Sorin, encased him in stone at Markov Manor, and planeswalked away.

ori.text: In Magic Origins, Nahiri wakes from her long slumber when the Eldrazi stir, and as Zendikar breaks open she senses that their prison has been opened.
She frees herself from her cocoon and sends a summons to Sorin and the Spirit Dragon, but they never come, and she realizes she is alone.
She crushes Eldrazi with an avalanche, visits the hedron network's sites, and decides she "would do it alone."

Near the Eye of Ugin she fights and kills vampires, discovers that their sacrifices had disrupted the network, and reshapes a statue of Ulamog into a new hedron that repairs the prison and drives the titans back into torpor.

soi.text: In Shadows over Innistrad, Nahiri has come to Innistrad with a grudge, and she vows to take everything from Sorin.
Her machinations drive Avacyn and most of the angels insane, fragmenting the Church, and she bends stone gargoyles to her will.
Sorin recruits Olivia Voldaren against her, and after Nahiri defeats Sorin and encases him in stone, Olivia proclaims herself lord of Innistrad.

In a flashback, Nahiri fights Sorin beside the Helvault and is bested when he disarms her and holds a blade to her throat, and the ghoul-raiser Gisa later befriends her after Nahiri cuts down her summoned ghouls.

emn.text: In Eldritch Moon, Nahiri confronts Sorin, telling him she resealed the Eldrazi prison alone after neither he nor Ugin answered her signal, and accuses him of abandoning her.
Sorin dismisses her, saying he molded her, and when she forges a sword and demands he return with her to Zendikar, he disarms her and hurls her into the Helvault.
Freed when the Helvault shatters, she finds Zendikar in ruins with the three titans loose, and swears that "As Zendikar has bled, so will Innistrad."

She calls Emrakul to Innistrad, and in the final confrontation she declares she is "done being a warden," turns Emrakul's monsters on the vampires, and traps Sorin in a stone cocoon before planeswalking away.

znr.text: In Zendikar Rising, Nahiri returns to Zendikar determined to rid it of the Roil, and in the heart of the Skyclave she takes the key and reveals she is after the last lithoform core.

She hires Akiri's party to retrieve the Core from a Murasa Skyclave, claiming it will heal Zendikar, but once she has it she uses it to destroy an elemental and pushes the paralyzed Akiri off a ledge.
Nissa, who thinks the plane must not be torn apart, fights her, and Jace seeks her out in the Singing City and later takes control of her mind.
In the end, Nissa merges her magic with the Core, colliding with Nahiri's hedrons and flattening the Singing City, and she restores Zendikar while Nahiri swears revenge on Jace.

one.text: In Phyrexia: All Will Be One, Nahiri joins the strike force that infiltrates New Phyrexia, where a planar shield scatters them and she is scratched on the neck.
She helps cut a Zendikari prince free of living cables and catches the falling earth with her magic as the group drops down to Mirrodin.
She soon realizes that the scratch has become a Phyrexian spike, hides her infection to get her companions as far as she can, and chooses to fight on rather than be healed.

In the coliseum, with her infection spreading, Nahiri declares that the mission only goes forward if they move on, then tears apart Sheoldred's Coliseum with her last free breath, sacrificing herself, and Elesh Norn compleats her.

mom.text: In March of the Machine, a compleated Nahiri brings the bound Sheoldred to Elesh Norn, who has her encase three planeswalkers in stone, and Nahiri vows to wake the weapon on Zendikar.
On Zendikar, she smothers the Roil's attacks, uses the Emeria Skyclave to connect the hedron networks, and fuses herself into its heart as its keystone.
Tazri sends Akiri's party after her, and Nahiri's stone attacks beat them back until Tazri hurls the halo at the entombed planeswalker.
The keystone breaks and Nahiri crumbles from the stone as the Emeria Skyclave falls to the earth with her trapped inside.

mat.text: In The Aftermath, Nahiri wakes after the invasion, tears the Phyrexian taint from her body and the Skyclave, and realizes she is no longer a Planeswalker.
She finds a hidden hedron holding her spark and climbs out into sunlight with new hope, resolving to restore her spark.
When Ajani appears and proposes making amends together, she suspects he has come to kill her and refuses.

The Skyclave dome collapses and she falls onto the hedron, crushing it and her last hope of regaining her power, so Nahiri blames planeswalkers for Zendikar's ruin and vows that none will set foot there again.
